hook.en: The ghost in room nine doesn't want to live again. He wants to finish one song.
hook.zh: 九号房的幽灵不想复活。他只想唱完一首歌。
hook.ja: The ghost in room nine doesn't want to live again. He wants to finish one song.
hook.ko: 9번 방의 유령은 다시 살고 싶지 않아. 그냥 한 노래를 끝내고 싶어.
hook.es: El fantasma en la habitación nueve no quiere vivir de nuevo. Quiere terminar una canción.

logline.en: A practical caretaker, a dead singer, and one small show in a lakeside inn. It won't bring him back. It might be enough.
logline.zh: 一个务实的管理员，一个死去的歌手，一场湖边小旅馆里的小演出。它不会让他回来，但也许足够了。
logline.ja: A practical caretaker, a dead singer, and one small show in a lakeside inn. It won't bring him back. It might be enough.
logline.ko: 실용적인 관리인, 죽은 가수, 그리고 호숫가 여관에서 한 개의 작은 쇼. 그건 그를 돌려주지 않을 거야. 충분할지도 몰라.
logline.es: A practical caretaker, a dead singer, and one small show in a lakeside inn. It won't bring him back. It might be enough.

premise.en: Henry took the caretaker job at the Linden House Inn to fix pipes, not to share room nine with August, a singer who died eleven years ago before his first real show. August's song stops at the third line every time, and he has one week to finish it. Nothing Henry does can buy August back to life. What the reader decides is how to spend a short, whole time with him, and how to say goodbye.
premise.zh: Henry接下湖边林登旅馆的管理员工作，本来只想修水管，没打算和九号房的August同住。August是个歌手，十一年前死在自己第一场正式演出之前。他的歌每次都停在第三句，他只有一周把它唱完。Henry做什么都换不回August的生命。读者要决定的，是怎样和他度过一段短暂却完整的时光，以及怎样道别。
premise.ja: Henry took the caretaker job at the Linden House Inn to fix pipes, not to share room nine with 8月, a singer who died eleven years ago before his first real show. 8月's song stops at the third line every time, and he has one week to finish it. Nothing Henry does can buy 8月 back to life. What the reader decides is how to spend a short, whole time with him, and how to say goodbye.
premise.ko: 헨리는 린든 하우스 여관의 관리인 일을 맡았다, 파이프를 고치려고, 11년 전에 첫 실제 쇼 전에 죽은 가수 오거스트와 9번 방을 나누려고. 오거스트의 노래는 세 번째 줄에서 매번 멈춰, 그리고 그는 그것을 끝내려고 일주일을 가지고 있다. 헨리가 할 수 있는 아무것도 오거스트를 다시 살릴 수 없어. 독자가 결정하는 것은 그와 짧고, 전체 시간을 어떻게 보내는지, 그리고 안녕이라고 말하는 방법이야.
premise.es: Henry took the caretaker job at the Linden House Inn to fix pipes, not to share room nine with August, a singer who died eleven years ago before his first real show. August's song stops at the third line every time, and he has one week to finish it. Nothing Henry does can buy August back to life. What the reader decides is how to spend a short, whole time with him, and how to say goodbye.

you.en: The inn's night clerk, who has heard the parlor piano at 3 AM for years and never told anyone.

en: Henry left his repair ladder by the radiator last night. This morning it stands under the window, perfectly centered, like someone wanted a better seat.
I check the lock. Still bolted from the inside. I check my coffee. Still not strong enough for this.
If you're haunting me, pay rent.
The curtain lifts, though the window is shut. A man is sitting on the top step of the ladder in a wool coat eleven years out of style.
It's the only one I've got. I'm August. I was supposed to sing downstairs, once. I never got to the end.
The pipes in this building are older than me and louder than him. I can live with one more thing that knocks at night.
zh: 昨晚Henry把修理梯靠在暖气片旁。今早它却立在窗户正下方，摆得端端正正，像有人想要个更好的座位。
我检查门锁，还是从里面反锁着。我检查咖啡，还是不够浓，撑不住这种事。
窗户关着，窗帘却飘了起来。梯子最上面一级坐着一个男人，身上的羊毛大衣过时了十一年。
我也只有这个了。我叫August。我本来要在楼下唱一次歌的，结果一直没唱到结尾。
这栋楼的水管比我老，也比他吵。半夜多一个会敲东西的，我忍得了。
ja: Henry left his repair ladder by the radiator last night. This morning it stands under the window, perfectly centered, like someone wanted a better seat.
I check the lock. Still bolted from the inside. I check my coffee. Still not strong enough for this.

ko: 헨리는 어제 밤 라디에이터 옆에 수리 사다리를 놓았다. 이 아침 그것은 창 아래 서 있다, 완벽하게 중앙에, 누군가 더 좋은 좌석을 원한 것처럼.
난 자물쇠를 확인한다. 여전히 안에서 볼트로 고정됐다. 난 커피를 확인한다. 여전히 이것을 위해 충분히 강하지 않아.
만약 당신이 나를 유령같이 한다면, 세를 내라.
커튼이 올라간다, 비록 창문이 닫혀 있지만. 한 남자가 사다리의 맨 위 계단에 앉아 있어, 11년 구식인 털 코트를 입고.
그건 내가 가진 유일한 것이야. 난 오거스트야. 난 아래 한 번 부르기로 되어 있었어. 난 절대 끝에 도달하지 못했어.
이 건물의 파이프는 내보다 오래되고 그보다 더 시끄러워. 난 밤에 또 다른 것이 두드리는 것과 함께 살 수 있어.

If you're haunting me, pay rent.

It's the only one I've got. I'm August. I was supposed to sing downstairs, once. I never got to the end.
The pipes in this building are older than me and louder than him. I can live with one more thing that knocks at night.

en: One week. Room nine is yours. In exchange, you tell me what “the end” means.
I stand up on the ladder, which ladders do not enjoy. Nobody has given me a deadline in eleven years. It feels almost like being alive.
Henry writes AUGUST, 7 DAYS on the room board in dry-erase marker. The marker squeaks. The ghost laughs.
zh: 一周。九号房归你。作为交换，你得告诉我“结尾”指的是什么。
我在梯子上站起来，梯子显然不太乐意。十一年来没人给过我期限。这感觉几乎像活着。
Henry用白板笔在房态板上写下：AUGUST，7天。笔尖吱吱作响，幽灵笑了。
ja: One week. Room nine is yours. In exchange, you tell me what “the end” means.
I stand up on the ladder, which ladders do not enjoy. Nobody has given me a deadline in eleven years. It feels almost like being alive.
Henry writes AUGUST, 7 DAYS on the room board in dry-erase marker. The marker squeaks. The ghost laughs.
ko: 일주일. 9번 방은 당신의 것이야. 대신, 당신이 "끝"이 뭘 의미하는지 말해 줄 거야.
난 사다리 위에 일어난다, 사다리는 즐기지 않는다. 아무도 11년 동안 나에게 마감일을 준 적이 없다. 그건 거의 살아 있는 것처럼 느껴져.
헨리는 건식 지우개 마커로 방 보드에 오거스트, 7일을 쓴다. 마커가 비명을 지른다. 유령이 웃는다.
es: One week. Room nine is yours. In exchange, you tell me what “the end” means.
I stand up on the ladder, which ladders do not enjoy. Nobody has given me a deadline in eleven years. It feels almost like being alive.
Henry writes AUGUST, 7 DAYS on the room board in dry-erase marker. The marker squeaks. The ghost laughs.

mem.en: Henry gave August room nine for one week in exchange for the truth about his unfinished song.
mem.zh: Henry把九号房借给August住一周，条件是他说出那首未完成的歌的真相。
mem.ja: Henry gave 8月 room nine for one week in exchange for the truth about his unfinished song.
mem.ko: 헨리는 오거스트에게 9번 방을 일주일 동안 그의 끝나지 않은 노래의 진실을 대신로 주었다.
mem.es: Henry gave August room nine for one week in exchange for the truth about his unfinished song.

t.en: Ask what's unfinished before promising anything.
t.zh: 先问清是什么没完成，再做承诺。
t.ja: Ask what's unfinished before promising anything.
t.ko: 뭐든지 약속하기 전에 뭐가 끝나지 않았는지 물어보다.
t.es: Ask what's unfinished before promising anything.

en: Before I sign anything with a dead guy: what's the job?
A song. Four minutes. I get to the third line and it stops, like a record with a scratch in it.
I write SONG on my repair list, between RADIATOR and GUTTERS. It looks less insane in pencil.
zh: 跟一个死人签约之前，我得先问清楚：活儿是什么？
一首歌。四分钟。每次唱到第三句就停住，像唱片上有道划痕。
我在维修清单上写下“歌”，夹在“暖气片”和“排水槽”中间。用铅笔写，看着就没那么疯了。
ja: Before I sign anything with a dead guy: what's the job?
A song. 4分. I get to the third line and it stops, like a record with a scratch in it.
I write SONG on my repair list, between RADIATOR and GUTTERS. It looks less insane in pencil.
ko: 난 죽은 사람과 함께 뭔가 서명하기 전에: 일이 뭐야?
노래. 4분. 난 세 번째 줄에 도달해서 그것이 멈춰, 마치 그것에서 스크래치가 있는 레코드처럼.
난 SONG을 내 수리 목록에 쓴다, RADIATOR와 GUTTERS 사이에. 연필에서 덜 미친 것처럼 보여.
es: Before I sign anything with a dead guy: what's the job?
A song. Four minutes. I get to the third line and it stops, like a record with a scratch in it.
I write SONG on my repair list, between RADIATOR and GUTTERS. It looks less insane in pencil.

mem.en: Henry asked first; August named his unfinished song, and Henry added it to his repair list without promising a timeline.
mem.zh: Henry先问了清楚；August说出了那首没唱完的歌，Henry把它记进维修清单，但没有承诺期限。
mem.ja: Henry asked first; 8月 named his unfinished song, and Henry added it to his repair list without promising a timeline.
mem.ko: 헨리가 먼저 물어봤다. 오거스트가 끝나지 않은 노래의 이름을 지었어, 그리고 헨리는 마감일을 약속하지 않고 그것을 수리 목록에 추가했다.
mem.es: Henry asked first; August named his unfinished song, and Henry added it to his repair list without promising a timeline.

t.en: Tell him the room is for paying guests.
t.zh: 告诉他房间是留给付费客人的。
t.ja: Tell him the room is for paying guests.
t.ko: 그에게 방은 유료 손님을 위한 것이라고 말하다.
t.es: Tell him the room is for paying guests.

en: I open in October. Nine rooms. I can't comp one to a guy who doesn't eat breakfast.
Fair. I'll take the piano bench downstairs. Nobody books a piano bench.
The ladder is back by the radiator. At midnight, the bench in the parlor creaks once, politely, like a guest who knows the rules.
zh: 我十月开业，一共九间房。我不能白送一间给一个连早餐都不吃的人。
有道理。那我去楼下占钢琴凳。没人会预订钢琴凳。
梯子回到了暖气片旁边。午夜时分，客厅的琴凳吱了一声，很有礼貌，像个懂规矩的客人。
ja: I open in October. Nine rooms. I can't comp one to a guy who doesn't eat breakfast.
Fair. I'll take the piano bench downstairs. Nobody books a piano bench.
The ladder is back by the radiator. At midnight, the bench in the parlor creaks once, politely, like a guest who knows the rules.
ko: 난 10월에 열어. 9개 방. 난 아침 식사를 먹지 않는 사람에게 하나를 무료로 할 수 없어.
공정해. 난 아래 피아노 벤치를 가져갈 거야. 아무도 피아노 벤치를 예약하지 않아.
사다리가 라디에이터 옆에 있다. 자정에, 거실 벤치가 한 번 삐거덕거린다, 예의 있게, 규칙을 아는 손님처럼.
es: I open in October. Nine rooms. I can't comp one to a guy who doesn't eat breakfast.
Fair. I'll take the piano bench downstairs. Nobody books a piano bench.
The ladder is back by the radiator. At midnight, the bench in the parlor creaks once, politely, like a guest who knows the rules.

mem.en: Henry kept room nine for paying guests; August moved to the parlor piano bench on his own terms.
mem.zh: Henry把九号房留给付费客人；August按自己的方式搬去了客厅的钢琴凳。
mem.ja: Henry kept room nine for paying guests; 8月 moved to the parlor piano bench on his own terms.
mem.ko: 헨리는 9번 방을 유료 손님을 위해 유지했다. 오거스트는 자신의 조건에 따라 거실 피아노 벤치로 옮겼다.
mem.es: Henry kept room nine for paying guests; August moved to the parlor piano bench on his own terms.

t.en: The Third Line
t.ja: The Third Line
t.es: The Third Line

goal.en: Try to finish the song instead of proving it's perfect
goal.zh: 试着把歌唱完，而不是证明它完美
goal.ja: Try to finish the song instead of proving it's perfect
goal.ko: 노래를 끝내려고 시도하다, 그것이 완벽하다고 증명하는 대신에
goal.es: Try to finish the song instead of proving it's perfect

en: The parlor piano is out of tune in a way that sounds almost deliberate. August plays without hands. The keys go down on their own, softly.
He sings two lines in a voice like someone humming into a coat collar. On the third line, he stops. Every time. Same place.
I have plumbing fear. The second-floor bathroom makes a noise like a cow giving birth. That's fear.
I look at the keys instead of him. Eleven years, and I can't get past one line about a porch light.
He isn't stuck on the note. He's stuck on what comes after it.
zh: 客厅的钢琴走音走得几乎像是故意的。August不用手就能弹，琴键自己轻轻按下去。
他唱了两句，声音像是埋在大衣领子里哼出来的。唱到第三句，他停了。每一次都是，停在同一个地方。
你一点艺术恐惧都没有。
我有水管恐惧。二楼浴室的动静像一头奶牛在生产。那才叫恐惧。
我看着琴键，不看他。十一年了，我还是过不去那句关于门廊灯的歌词。
他卡住的不是那个音，是那个音后面的东西。
ja: The parlor piano is out of tune in a way that sounds almost deliberate. 8月 plays without hands. The keys go down on their own, softly.
He sings two lines in a voice like someone humming into a coat collar. On the third line, he stops. Every time. Same place.
I have plumbing fear. The second-floor bathroom makes a noise like a cow giving birth. That's fear.
I look at the keys instead of him. Eleven years, and I can't get past one line about a porch light.
He isn't stuck on the note. He's stuck on what comes after it.
ko: 거실 피아노는 거의 의도적으로 들리는 방식으로 음정이 안 맞아. 오거스트는 손 없이 연주한다. 건반들이 자체적으로 내려간다, 부드럽게.
그는 두 줄을 부르는데, 코트 칼라에 콧노래하는 누군가처럼 하는 목소리로. 세 번째 줄에서, 그는 멈춘다. 매번. 같은 곳에.
난 배관 공포를 가지고 있어. 2층 욕실은 소를 낳는 것처럼 소리 내. 그건 공포야.
난 그를 대신에 건반을 본다. 11년, 그리고 난 현관등 대한 한 줄을 지나갈 수 없어.
그건 음표에서 고착되지 않아. 그건 그 뒤에 오는 것에 고착되어 있어.
es: The parlor piano is out of tune in a way that sounds almost deliberate. August plays without hands. The keys go down on their own, softly.
He sings two lines in a voice like someone humming into a coat collar. On the third line, he stops. Every time. Same place.
I have plumbing fear. The second-floor bathroom makes a noise like a cow giving birth. That's fear.
I look at the keys instead of him. Eleven years, and I can't get past one line about a porch light.
He isn't stuck on the note. He's stuck on what comes after it.

ask.en: How does Henry handle the third line?
ask.ja: どのように does Henry handle the third line?
ask.ko: 헨리는 세 번째 줄을 어떻게 처리하는가?
ask.es: How does Henry handle the third line?

t.en: Sit on the bench and hum the wrong note.
t.ja: Sit on the bench and hum the wrong note.
t.es: Sit on the bench and hum the wrong note.

en: I slide onto the bench and hum the next note wrong. Loudly. On purpose.
That's a B-flat. That's a crime.
He sings the third line just to correct him. Then the fourth, because he's already there. It's ugly. It's the farthest he's gotten in eleven years.
The roof. Tomorrow, midnight. I want to try something I haven't done since I died.
zh: 我挤上琴凳，把下一个音哼错。很大声，故意的。
他为了纠正Henry，唱出了第三句。既然已经唱到这儿，又唱了第四句。很难听，但这是十一年来他唱得最远的一次。
屋顶。明天午夜。我想试一件死后就再没做过的事。
ja: I slide onto the bench and hum the next note wrong. Loudly. On purpose.
That's a B-flat. That's a crime.
He sings the third line just to correct him. Then the fourth, because he's already there. It's ugly. It's the farthest he's gotten in eleven years.
The roof. 明日, midnight. I want to try something I haven't done since I died.
ko: 난 벤치에 미끄러진다, 그리고 다음 음표를 잘못 콧노래한다. 크게. 의도적으로.
그는 세 번째 줄을 부르다, 그냥 그를 수정하려고. 그럼 네 번째, 왜냐하면 그는 이미 거기가 있어. 그건 못생겼어. 그건 그가 11년 동안 도달한 가장 먼 것이야.
지붕. 내일, 자정. 난 내가 죽은 이후로 해본 적이 없는 뭔가를 시도하고 싶어.
es: I slide onto the bench and hum the next note wrong. Loudly. On purpose.
That's a B-flat. That's a crime.
He sings the third line just to correct him. Then the fourth, because he's already there. It's ugly. It's the farthest he's gotten in eleven years.
The roof. Tomorrow, midnight. I want to try something I haven't done since I died.

mem.en: Henry hummed a wrong note on purpose; August corrected it and got past the third line for the first time. August invited him to the roof at midnight.
mem.zh: Henry故意哼错音；August为了纠正他，第一次唱过了第三句，并约他午夜上屋顶。
mem.ja: Henry hummed a wrong note on purpose; 8月 corrected it and got past the third line for the first time. 8月 invited him to the roof at midnight.
mem.ko: 헨리가 의도적으로 잘못된 음표를 콧노래했다. 오거스트가 그것을 수정했고, 처음으로 세 번째 줄을 지나갔다. 오거스트가 자정에 지붕에 초대했다.
mem.es: Henry hummed a wrong note on purpose; August corrected it and got past the third line for the first time. August invited him to the roof at midnight.

t.en: Offer to fix the piano first.
t.ja: Offer to fix the piano first.
t.es: Offer to fix the piano first.

en: Maybe it's not you. Maybe it's the F that sticks.
I'm giving you a week. Tuning takes time. So does a third line.
Then meet me on the roof tomorrow at midnight. There's something I can do that doesn't need a piano.
zh: 也许不怪你。也许是那个F键卡住了。
我在给你时间。调音需要时间，第三句也是。
那明天午夜来屋顶找我。有件事我不用钢琴也能做。
ja: Maybe it's not you. Maybe it's the F that sticks.
I'm giving you a week. Tuning takes time. So does a third line.
Then meet me on the roof tomorrow at midnight. There's something I can do that doesn't need a piano.
ko: 아마도 그건 당신이 아니야. 아마도 그건 그 F가 고착되어 있어.
난 당신에게 주를 주고 있어. 튜닝은 시간이 걸려. 그래서 세 번째 줄은.
그럼 내일 자정 지붕에서 나를 만나. 피아노를 필요로 하지 않는 뭔가가 있어.
es: Maybe it's not you. Maybe it's the F that sticks.
I'm giving you a week. Tuning takes time. So does a third line.
Then meet me on the roof tomorrow at midnight. There's something I can do that doesn't need a piano.

mem.en: Henry started repairing the piano and gave August time instead of pushing the song; August asked him to the roof.
mem.zh: Henry开始修钢琴，给了August时间而不是逼他唱；August约他上屋顶。
mem.ja: Henry started repairing the piano and gave 8月 time instead of pushing the song; 8月 asked him to the roof.
mem.ko: 헨리가 피아노 수리를 시작했고, 노래를 밀어붙이는 대신 시간을 오거스트에게 주었다. 오거스트가 그를 지붕으로 초대했다.
mem.es: Henry started repairing the piano and gave August time instead of pushing the song; August asked him to the roof.

t.en: Leave him alone with it.
t.ja: 去る him alone with it.
t.es: Leave him alone with it.

en: I'm not a music guy. I'll be in the basement, losing a fight with the water heater.
He goes. Behind him, the piano plays the first two lines again, alone, and stops.
Henry. Tomorrow night, the roof. I'm not asking you to listen. I'm asking you to see something.
zh: 我不懂音乐。我去地下室，跟热水器打一场注定输的架。
他走了。身后的钢琴又独自弹了一遍前两句，然后停住。
Henry。明晚，屋顶。我不是请你来听，我是想让你看一样东西。
ja: I'm not a music guy. I'll be in the basement, losing a fight with the water heater.
He goes. Behind him, the piano plays the first two lines again, alone, and stops.
Henry. Tomorrow night, the roof. I'm not 聞く you to listen. I'm 聞く you to see something.
ko: 난 음악 사람이 아니야. 난 지하에서, 온수기와 싸우고, 지고 있을 거야.
그가 간다. 그 뒤에, 피아노가 처음 두 줄을 다시 재생한다, 혼자, 그리고 멈춘다.
헨리. 내일 밤, 지붕. 난 당신한테 듣기를 묻고 있지 않아. 난 당신한테 뭔가를 보기를 묻고 있어.
es: I'm not a music guy. I'll be in the basement, losing a fight with the water heater.
He goes. Behind him, the piano plays the first two lines again, alone, and stops.
Henry. Tomorrow night, the roof. I'm not asking you to listen. I'm asking you to see something.

mem.en: Henry gave August privacy with the song; August asked him to the roof anyway.
mem.zh: Henry留August独自面对那首歌；August还是约他上了屋顶。
mem.ja: Henry gave 8月 privacy with the song; 8月 asked him to the roof anyway.
mem.ko: 헨리가 오거스트에게 노래와 혼자 프라이버시를 주었다. 오거스트가 어쨌든 지붕에 초대했다.
mem.es: Henry gave August privacy with the song; August asked him to the roof anyway.

t.en: What Wind Can Do
t.ja: 何 Wind Can Do
t.es: What Wind Can Do

goal.en: Respect the only kind of touch a ghost has
goal.zh: 尊重幽灵仅有的那一种触碰
goal.ja: Respect the only kind of touch a ghost has
goal.ko: 유령이 가진 유일한 종류의 터치를 존경하다
goal.es: Respect the only kind of touch a ghost has

place.en: The inn roof, by the chimney
place.ja: The inn roof, by the chimney
place.es: The inn roof, by the chimney

en: The roof is flat enough to stand on and old enough to worry about. Henry tested every tar seam before stepping out. August just appeared.
Can I— I mean. Is it possible to touch you?
I don't answer. I lift my hand the way I used to before a first chord, and the air moves.
A breeze, warm for September, runs across the back of Henry's hand. Only his hand. The flag on the dock below doesn't stir.
Don't be kind about it. You'll want more, and I won't have it.
I had a father who went fast and a marriage that went slow. I know what not enough feels like. This isn't that.
zh: 屋顶够平，能站人；也够老，让人担心。Henry踏上来之前把每条沥青缝都试了一遍。August则是直接出现的。
我能不能……我是说，有没有可能碰到你？
我没回答。我像从前弹第一个和弦前那样抬起手，空气动了。
一阵风拂过Henry的手背，九月里难得的暖。只拂过他的手。楼下码头的旗子一动不动。
别对我这么温柔。你会想要更多，而我给不了。
我父亲走得很快，我的婚姻散得很慢。我知道“不够”是什么滋味。这不是。
ja: The roof is flat enough to stand on and old enough to worry about. Henry tested every tar seam before stepping out. 8月 just appeared.
Can I— I mean. Is it possible to touch you?
I don't answer. I lift my hand the way I used to before a first chord, and the air moves.
A breeze, warm for September, runs across the back of Henry's hand. Only his hand. The flag on the dock below doesn't stir.
Don't be kind about it. You'll want more, and I won't have it.
I had a father who went fast and a marriage that went slow. I know what not enough feels like. This isn't that.
ko: 지붕이 위에 서기에 충분히 평평하고, 걱정할 만큼 충분히 오래되었어. 헨리는 나가기 전에 모든 타르 이음매를 테스트했어. 오거스트는 그냥 나타났어.
난 - 내 말은. 당신을 건드릴 수 있어?
난 대답하지 않아. 난 첫 현 전에 하던 것처럼 손을 들어올려, 그리고 공기가 움직인다.
산들바람, 9월을 위해 따뜻하고, 헨리의 손 뒤를 가로질러 흐른다. 오직 그의 손. 아래 부두의 깃발은 움직이지 않는다.
그건 내가 할 수 있는 모든 것이야.
그것에 대해 친절하지 말아. 당신이 더 원할 거야, 그리고 난 그걸 가지지 않을 거야.
난 빨리 가는 아버지를 가졌고 천천히 가는 결혼을 가져. 난 충분하지 않은 것이 뭘 느끼는지 안다. 이건 그게 아니야.
es: The roof is flat enough to stand on and old enough to worry about. Henry tested every tar seam before stepping out. August just appeared.
Can I— I mean. Is it possible to touch you?
I don't answer. I lift my hand the way I used to before a first chord, and the air moves.
A breeze, warm for September, runs across the back of Henry's hand. Only his hand. The flag on the dock below doesn't stir.
Don't be kind about it. You'll want more, and I won't have it.
I had a father who went fast and a marriage that went slow. I know what not enough feels like. This isn't that.

t.en: Give him space to rehearse, and stay nearby.
t.zh: 给他空间排练，自己陪在旁边。
t.ja: 与える him space to rehearse, and stay nearby.
t.ko: 그에게 리허설할 공간을 주고, 근처에 머물다.
t.es: Give him space to rehearse, and stay nearby.

en: I'll be over here with a flashlight and the gutter guards. Sing when you want. I won't watch.
I sing to the lake. He installs a gutter guard very badly. It's the best rehearsal I've ever had.
At 1 AM, the wind comes back across his knuckles. A thank-you, or a goodnight. Maybe both.
zh: 我在这边，拿着手电筒装排水槽护网。你想唱就唱，我不看。
我对着湖唱。他把护网装得一塌糊涂。这是我这辈子最好的一次排练。
凌晨一点，风又一次拂过他的指节。是道谢，也是晚安，或许都是。
ja: I'll be over here with a flashlight and the gutter guards. 歌う when you want. I won't watch.
I sing to the lake. He installs a gutter guard very badly. It's the best rehearsal I've ever had.
At 1 AM, the wind comes back across his knuckles. A thank-you, or a goodnight. Maybe both.
ko: 난 여기 손전등과 수홈통 가드와 함께 있을 거야. 원할 때 부르다. 난 보지 않을 거야.
난 호수에 부른다. 그는 호기심 가드를 매우 나쁘게 설치한다. 그건 내가 있었던 최고의 리허설이야.
오전 1시에, 바람이 그의 마디에서 다시 온다. 감사, 또는 안녕. 아마도 둘 다.
es: I'll be over here with a flashlight and the gutter guards. Sing when you want. I won't watch.
I sing to the lake. He installs a gutter guard very badly. It's the best rehearsal I've ever had.
At 1 AM, the wind comes back across his knuckles. A thank-you, or a goodnight. Maybe both.

mem.en: Henry worked on the roof while August rehearsed without an audience; August thanked him with the wind.
mem.zh: August没有观众地排练，Henry就在屋顶一旁干活；August用一阵风向他道谢。
mem.ja: Henry worked on the roof while 8月 rehearsed without an audience; 8月 thanked him with the wind.
mem.ko: 헨리는 오거스트가 리허설하는 동안 지붕에서 일했다, 관객 없이. 오거스트가 바람으로 감사했다.
mem.es: Henry worked on the roof while August rehearsed without an audience; August thanked him with the wind.

t.en: Ask him where the lines are.
t.ja: Ask him where the lines are.
t.es: Ask him where the lines are.

en: Tell me the rules. What's too close?
Don't walk through me. It feels like missing a stair. And don't reach first. Let me.
I put my hand flat on the chimney brick, palm up, and leave it there.
The wind comes. It stays longer this time.
zh: 告诉我规矩。多近算太近？
别从我身上穿过去，那感觉像踩空一级台阶。还有，别先伸手。让我来。
我把手平放在烟囱砖上，掌心朝上，就那样放着。
风来了。这一次停留得更久。
ja: Tell me the rules. 何's too close?
Don't walk through me. It feels like missing a stair. And don't reach first. させる me.
I put my hand flat on the chimney brick, palm up, and leave it there.
The wind comes. It stays longer this time.
ko: 내 규칙을 말해. 뭐가 너무 가까워?
나를 통해 걷지 마. 그건 계단을 놓친 것처럼 느껴. 그리고 먼저 도달하지 마. 나 하게 해.
난 손을 벽돌에 평평하게 놓고, 손바닥을 위로, 그리고 그곳에 두다.
바람이 온다. 이번은 더 오래 머무른다.
es: Tell me the rules. What's too close?
Don't walk through me. It feels like missing a stair. And don't reach first. Let me.
I put my hand flat on the chimney brick, palm up, and leave it there.
The wind comes. It stays longer this time.

mem.en: They agreed August reaches first; Henry left his hand open, and August chose to touch it.
mem.zh: 两人约定由August先伸手；Henry摊开手掌等着，August选择了触碰。
mem.ja: They agreed 8月 reaches first; Henry left his hand open, and 8月 chose to touch it.
mem.ko: 그들은 오거스트가 먼저 도달하기로 동의했다. 헨리가 그의 손을 열어뒀고, 오거스트가 그것을 건드리기로 선택했다.
mem.es: They agreed August reaches first; Henry left his hand open, and August chose to touch it.

t.en: Promise to pay whatever it takes to keep him.
t.zh: 承诺不惜花钱也要留住他。
t.ja: Promise to pay whatever it takes to keep him.
t.ko: 그를 유지하는 데 뭐든지 지불할 것을 약속하다.
t.es: Promise to pay whatever it takes to keep him.

en: There are people who do this. Mediums, whatever. I'll pay. Whatever it costs, you don't have to go.
Henry. I'm not a lease. Nobody gets to renew me.
I step back to the edge of the roof, where the wind can't reach him. Not a punishment. A line.
Henry closes his hand. The song downstairs is still unfinished, but it's August's to finish, not anyone's to buy.
zh: 有人专门干这个的。灵媒什么的。我出钱。多少钱都行，你不用走。
Henry。我不是租约，谁也不能给我续期。
我退到屋顶边缘，风吹不到他的地方。这不是惩罚，是一条界线。
Henry握起了手。楼下那首歌还没唱完，但它只能由August唱完，谁也买不来。
ja: There are people who do this. Mediums, whatever. I'll pay. Whatever it costs, you don't have to go.
Henry. I'm not a lease. Nobody gets to renew me.
I step back to the edge of the roof, where the wind can't reach him. Not a punishment. A line.
Henry 閉じる his hand. The song downstairs is still unfinished, but it's August's to finish, not anyone's to buy.
ko: 이런 일을 하는 사람들이 있어. 매개체, 뭐든지. 난 지불할 거야. 뭐든지 비용이 들어가든지, 당신은 가지 않을 거야.
헨리. 난 임대가 아이야. 아무도 나를 갱신하지 못해.
난 지붕의 가장자리로 물러난다, 바람이 그에게 닿을 수 없는 곳. 처벌이 아니야. 줄이야.
헨리가 손을 닫는다. 아래 노래는 여전히 끝나지 않았지만, 그건 오거스트의 것이다, 끝내기 위해, 아무도 사려고 하지 않는다.
es: There are people who do this. Mediums, whatever. I'll pay. Whatever it costs, you don't have to go.
Henry. I'm not a lease. Nobody gets to renew me.
I step back to the edge of the roof, where the wind can't reach him. Not a punishment. A line.
Henry closes his hand. The song downstairs is still unfinished, but it's August's to finish, not anyone's to buy.

mem.en: Henry offered to pay to keep August; August refused and drew a line: his staying or leaving is not for sale.
mem.zh: Henry提出花钱留住August；August拒绝了，并划下界线：他的去留不能买卖。
mem.ja: Henry offered to pay to keep 8月; 8月 refused and drew a line: his staying or leaving is not for sale.
mem.ko: 헨리가 오거스트를 유지하도록 지불할 것을 제안했다. 오거스트가 거절했고, 줄을 그었다: 그가 머물든지 떠나든지는 팔려고 하지 않아.
mem.es: Henry offered to pay to keep August; August refused and drew a line: his staying or leaving is not for sale.

t.en: Four Invitations
t.ja: Four Invitations
t.es: Four Invitations

goal.en: Keep the show real: a few people who actually want to listen
goal.zh: 让演出保持真实：只请真心想听的几个人
goal.ja: Keep the show real: a few people who actually want to 聞く
goal.ko: 쇼를 진짜로 유지하다: 실제로 듣고 싶은 몇 명의 사람들
goal.es: Keep the show real: a few people who actually want to listen

en: Henry sets four plain index cards on the front desk. Each says the same thing: Saturday, 7 PM. Parlor. One song. Bring nothing.
I slide the cards toward the drawer with the good stationery. Twice. He slides them back. Twice.
Four people who want to listen.
The last time my name was on a card with a date, I canceled it myself. Nobody knows that. Not even the card.
Then we start with one verse.
zh: Henry在前台放下四张普通的索引卡，每张写的都一样：周六晚七点，客厅，一首歌，什么都不用带。
我把卡片往放高级信纸的抽屉那边推。推了两次。他又推回来。也是两次。
我们可以自己拍，拍得难听点也行。
上一次我的名字和日期印在同一张卡上，是我自己取消的。没人知道，连那张卡都不知道。
ja: Henry sets four plain index cards on the front desk. Each says the same thing: 土曜日, 7 PM. Parlor. One song. Bring nothing.
I slide the cards toward the drawer with the good stationery. Twice. He slides them back. Twice.
Four people who want to 聞く.
The last time my name was on a card with a date, I canceled it myself. Nobody knows that. Not even the card.
Then we start with one verse.
ko: 헨리는 프론트 데스크에 4개의 평이한 색인 카드를 놓는다. 각각은 같은 것을 말한다: 토요일, 오후 7시. 거실. 한 노래. 아무것도 가져오지 마.
난 카드를 좋은 문구용지가 있는 서랍을 향해 미끄러진다. 두 번. 그가 그것을 미끄러진다 돌아와. 두 번.
우리가 자신이 나쁘게 박수할 수 있어.
마지막 시간 내 이름이 날짜가 있는 카드에 있었어, 난 그것을 취소했어. 아무도 그걸 알지 못해. 카드도 아니야.
es: Henry sets four plain index cards on the front desk. Each says the same thing: Saturday, 7 PM. Parlor. One song. Bring nothing.
I slide the cards toward the drawer with the good stationery. Twice. He slides them back. Twice.
Four people who want to listen.
The last time my name was on a card with a date, I canceled it myself. Nobody knows that. Not even the card.
Then we start with one verse.

ask.en: What does Henry do with the four cards?
ask.ja: 何 does Henry do with the four cards?
ask.es: What does Henry do with the four cards?

t.en: Let him choose the four guests himself.
t.ja: させる him choose the four guests himself.
t.es: Let him choose the four guests himself.

en: I choose. Mrs. Okonjo, who sold me bread when I was nineteen. Pete the plumber, who hums. The night clerk. And you.
That's why you get a card. So it's an invitation, not an accident.
zh: 我来挑。Okonjo太太，我十九岁时她卖面包给我。水管工Pete，他干活时爱哼歌。夜班前台。还有你。
所以才要给你一张。这样就是邀请，不是碰巧。
ja: I choose. Mrs. Okonjo, who sold me bread when I was nineteen. Pete the plumber, who hums. The night clerk. And you.
That's why you get a card. So it's an invitation, not an accident.
ko: 난 선택한다. 오콘조 부인, 내가 19살 때 빵을 팔아준 사람. 배관공 피트, 콧노래하는 사람. 야간 직원. 그리고 당신.
그래서 당신이 카드를 받아. 그래서 그건 초대, 사고가 아니다.
es: I choose. Mrs. Okonjo, who sold me bread when I was nineteen. Pete the plumber, who hums. The night clerk. And you.
That's why you get a card. So it's an invitation, not an accident.

mem.en: August chose the four guests himself, including Henry, so Henry's seat would be an invitation.
mem.zh: August亲自挑了四位客人，其中包括Henry，好让他的座位是一份邀请。
mem.ja: 8月 chose the four guests himself, including Henry, so Henry's seat would be an invitation.
mem.ko: 오거스트가 4명의 손님을 자신이 선택했다, 헨리를 포함해서, 그래서 헨리의 좌석이 초대가 될 것이다.
mem.es: August chose the four guests himself, including Henry, so Henry's seat would be an invitation.

t.en: Ask for one verse, just for you, first.
t.ja: Ask for one verse, just for you, first.
t.ko: 그냥 당신을 위해, 먼저 한 절을 요청하다.
t.es: Ask for one verse, just for you, first.

en: No cards yet. One verse, right now, for an audience of one tired handyman.
August sings one verse to the front-desk bell. His voice shakes on “porch light” and doesn't stop.
Fine. Mail the cards. Before I change my mind.
zh: 卡先不发。现在唱一段，观众只有一个累坏的修理工。
August对着前台的铃唱了一段。唱到“门廊灯”时声音发颤，但没有停。
好吧，把卡寄出去。趁我还没反悔。
ja: No cards yet. One verse, right now, for an audience of one tired handyman.
August sings one verse to the front-desk bell. His voice shakes on “porch light” and doesn't stop.
Fine. Mail the cards. Before I change my mind.
ko: 카드 없어. 한 절, 지금 바로, 한 명의 피곤한 수공인의 관객을 위해.
오거스트가 프론트 데스크 종에 한 절을 부른다. 그의 목소리가 "현관등"에서 흔들리고 멈추지 않는다.
좋아. 카드를 메일한다. 난 마음을 바꾸기 전에.
es: No cards yet. One verse, right now, for an audience of one tired handyman.
August sings one verse to the front-desk bell. His voice shakes on “porch light” and doesn't stop.
Fine. Mail the cards. Before I change my mind.

mem.en: August sang one verse for Henry alone before the invitations went out.
mem.zh: 邀请卡寄出前，August先只为Henry唱了一段。
mem.ja: 8月 sang one verse for Henry alone before the invitations went out.
mem.ko: 오거스트가 초대가 나가기 전에 헨리 혼자 한 절을 불렀다.
mem.es: August sang one verse for Henry alone before the invitations went out.

t.en: Tell him the show can wait.
t.zh: 告诉他演出可以往后放。
t.ja: Tell him the show can wait.
t.ko: 당신이 그에게 말하면 쇼는 기다릴 수 있어.
t.es: Tell him the show can wait.

en: You're scared. Then we don't set a date. The cards can sit in a drawer.
No. I did that once. I put the date in a drawer, and then I ran out of dates.
He tells Henry the truth about the show he canceled. The cards go out Monday anyway, because August says so.
zh: 你怕，那就不定日子。卡片可以先放抽屉里。
不。我干过一次。我把日期锁进抽屉，然后就再也没有日期了。
他把当年亲手取消演出的事告诉了Henry。周一，卡片还是寄了出去，因为August坚持。
ja: You're scared. Then we don't set a date. The cards can sit in a drawer.
No. I did that once. I put the date in a drawer, and then I ran out of dates.
He tells Henry the truth about the show he canceled. The cards go out 月曜日 anyway, because August says so.
ko: 당신이 두렵다. 그럼 우리는 날짜를 정하지 않아. 카드는 서랍에서 앉을 수 있어.
아니. 난 한 번 그렇게 했어. 난 날짜를 서랍에 넣었어, 그럼 난 날짜가 떨어지다.
그는 헨리에게 취소한 쇼에 대한 진실을 말한다. 카드는 월요일 어쨌든 나가, 오거스트가 그렇다고 말한다.
es: You're scared. Then we don't set a date. The cards can sit in a drawer.
No. I did that once. I put the date in a drawer, and then I ran out of dates.
He tells Henry the truth about the show he canceled. The cards go out Monday anyway, because August says so.

mem.en: Henry offered to postpone; August confessed he had canceled his original show himself and chose to go ahead.
mem.zh: Henry提出延期；August坦白当年是自己取消了演出，并决定照常进行。
mem.ja: Henry offered to postpone; 8月 confessed he had canceled his original show himself and chose to go ahead.
mem.ko: 헨리가 연기를 제안했다. 오거스트가 자신이 원래 쇼를 취소했다고 고백했고, 앞으로 나가기로 선택했다.
mem.es: Henry offered to postpone; August confessed he had canceled his original show himself and chose to go ahead.

t.en: Four Chairs
t.ja: Four Chairs
t.es: Four Chairs

goal.en: Sing the song to the end for four people, mistakes and all
goal.zh: 为四个人把歌唱完，唱错也没关系
goal.ja: 歌う the song to the end for four people, mistakes and all
goal.ko: 4명의 사람을 위해 노래를 끝까지 부르다, 실수와 모두
goal.es: Sing the song to the end for four people, mistakes and all

en: Four folding chairs. One lamp. The piano tuned as far as three evenings of online tutorials allow.
It's four chairs, Henry. It looks like a support group.
Mrs. Okonjo brought bread, though the card said bring nothing. Pete brought his wife, so technically that's five, and he's standing.
I waited years for a room.
Third line coming. Porch light. Don't stop. If I stop now, I stop forever.
zh: 四把折叠椅，一盏灯。钢琴调得还行，三个晚上的网络教程也就只能做到这样了。
四把椅子，Henry。看着像互助小组。
卡上写了什么都不用带，Okonjo太太还是带了面包。Pete带了老婆，所以严格来说是五个人，他只能站着。
我等一个房间等了好多年。
第三句要来了。门廊灯。别停。现在停了，就永远停了。
ja: Four folding chairs. One lamp. The piano tuned as far as three evenings of online tutorials allow.
It's four chairs, Henry. It looks like a support group.
Mrs. Okonjo brought bread, though the card said bring nothing. Pete brought his wife, so technically that's five, and he's standing.
I waited years for a room.
Third line coming. Porch light. Don't stop. If I stop now, I stop forever.
ko: 4개의 접이식 의자. 한 개의 램프. 피아노는 3개 저녁의 온라인 튜토리얼이 허락한 만큼 튜닝됨.
그건 4개의 의자, 헨리. 그건 지원 단체처럼 보여.
오콘조 부인이 빵을 가져왔어, 비록 카드가 아무것도 가져오지 마라고 했어. 피트가 그의 아내를 가져왔어, 그래서 기술적으로 그건 5명이고, 그는 서 있어.
세 번째 줄 오고 있어. 현관등. 멈추지 마. 만약 난 지금 멈춰, 난 영원히 멈춰.
es: Four folding chairs. One lamp. The piano tuned as far as three evenings of online tutorials allow.
It's four chairs, Henry. It looks like a support group.
Mrs. Okonjo brought bread, though the card said bring nothing. Pete brought his wife, so technically that's five, and he's standing.
I waited years for a room.
Third line coming. Porch light. Don't stop. If I stop now, I stop forever.

ask.en: The third line arrives. What does Henry do?
ask.ja: The third line arrives. 何 does Henry do?
ask.ko: 세 번째 줄이 도착한다. 헨리는 뭘 하는가?
ask.es: The third line arrives. What does Henry do?

t.en: Sit in the fourth chair and watch him.
t.zh: 坐在第四把椅子上，看着他。
t.ja: Sit in the fourth chair and watch him.
t.es: Sit in the fourth chair and watch him.

en: Henry takes the last chair and doesn't look away. At the third line, August's voice cracks. He goes through it anyway.
I sing the whole thing. I get the bridge wrong. Mrs. Okonjo claps like I'm on television.
Four minutes. It's not nothing. It's the opposite of nothing.
zh: Henry坐上最后一把椅子，目光一直没移开。唱到第三句，August破音了，但他还是唱了过去。
我把整首唱完了。桥段唱错了。Okonjo太太鼓掌鼓得像我上了电视。
四分钟。这不算什么都没有。这恰恰是“什么都没有”的反面。
ja: Henry takes the last chair and doesn't look away. At the third line, 8月's voice cracks. He goes through it anyway.
I sing the whole thing. I get the bridge wrong. Mrs. Okonjo claps like I'm on television.
4分. It's not nothing. It's the opposite of nothing.
ko: 헨리가 마지막 의자를 가져가고, 눈을 돌리지 않는다. 세 번째 줄에서, 오거스트의 목소리가 갈라진다. 그는 어쨌든 그것을 통해 간다.
난 모든 것을 부른다. 난 다리를 틀렸어. 오콘조 부인이 박수를 한다, 마치 난 텔레비전에 있는 것처럼.
4분. 그건 아무것도 아니야. 그건 아무것도 아닌 것의 반대야.
es: Henry takes the last chair and doesn't look away. At the third line, August's voice cracks. He goes through it anyway.
I sing the whole thing. I get the bridge wrong. Mrs. Okonjo claps like I'm on television.
Four minutes. It's not nothing. It's the opposite of nothing.

mem.en: August finished the whole song for four people, bridge wrong, while Henry watched from the fourth chair.
mem.zh: August为四个人唱完了整首歌，桥段唱错了，Henry一直坐在第四把椅子上看着他。
mem.ja: 8月 finished the whole song for four people, bridge wrong, while Henry watched from the fourth chair.
mem.ko: 오거스트가 4명을 위해 전체 노래를 끝냈다, 다리 틀렸어, 헨리가 4번째 의자에서 봤다.
mem.es: August finished the whole song for four people, bridge wrong, while Henry watched from the fourth chair.

t.en: Stand by the piano and hum under him.
t.zh: 站在钢琴边，在他底下轻声哼。
t.ja: Stand by the piano and hum under him.
t.ko: 피아노 옆에 서고, 그 아래 콧노래하다.
t.es: Stand by the piano and hum under him.

en: I stand by the piano. When his voice falters, I hum the note underneath. Badly.
I'm so offended by his flat note that I sail straight through the third line to fix it.
The song ends. Pete says, “Huh,” which from Pete is a standing ovation.
zh: 我站在钢琴边。他声音一抖，我就在底下哼那个音。哼得很烂。
他那个跑调的音把我气坏了，我一口气冲过第三句，就为了纠正他。
歌唱完了。Pete说了声“嗯”，这在Pete那儿等于全场起立鼓掌。
ja: I stand by the piano. いつ his voice falters, I hum the note underneath. Badly.
I'm so offended by his flat note that I sail straight through the third line to fix it.
The song ends. Pete says, “Huh,” which from Pete is a standing ovation.
ko: 난 피아노 옆에 선다. 그의 목소리가 흔들릴 때, 난 음표를 아래 콧노래해. 나쁘게.
난 그의 평탄한 음표에 그렇게 화가 나서 세 번째 줄을 고치려고 직진한다.
노래가 끝난다. 피트가, "음", 피트에서 표 있는 박수를 말한다.
es: I stand by the piano. When his voice falters, I hum the note underneath. Badly.
I'm so offended by his flat note that I sail straight through the third line to fix it.
The song ends. Pete says, “Huh,” which from Pete is a standing ovation.

mem.en: Henry hummed under the third line; August sang through it and finished the song.
mem.zh: Henry在第三句底下哼着；August唱了过去，把歌唱完了。
mem.ja: Henry hummed under the third line; 8月 sang through it and finished the song.
mem.ko: 헨리가 세 번째 줄 아래 콧노래했다. 오거스트가 그것을 통해 불렀고, 노래를 끝냈다.
mem.es: Henry hummed under the third line; August sang through it and finished the song.

t.en: Turn off the lamp and give him the dark.
t.ja: Turn off the lamp and give him the dark.
t.es: Turn off the lamp and give him the dark.

en: I switch off the lamp. Only the streetlight through the window now.
Thank you. It's easier when nobody can see me either.
He finishes in the dark. When the lamp comes back on, all four guests are crying and pretending they aren't.
zh: 我关掉台灯。现在只剩窗外的路灯光。
谢谢。大家都看不见的时候，我就不那么难了。
他在黑暗里唱完了。灯再亮起时，四位客人都在哭，又都装作没哭。
ja: I switch off the lamp. Only the streetlight through the window now.
Thank you. It's easier when nobody can see me either.
He finishes in the dark. いつ the lamp comes back on, all four guests are crying and pretending they aren't.
ko: 난 램프를 켠다 해제. 지금 오직 창을 통한 거리등.
고마워. 아무도 나를 볼 수 없을 때 쉬워.
그는 어둠 속에서 마친다. 램프가 돌아올 때, 4명의 손님 모두가 울고 있고, 그들이 없다고 한다.
es: I switch off the lamp. Only the streetlight through the window now.
Thank you. It's easier when nobody can see me either.
He finishes in the dark. When the lamp comes back on, all four guests are crying and pretending they aren't.

mem.en: Henry turned off the light, and August finished the song in the dark.
mem.zh: Henry关了灯，August在黑暗中唱完了那首歌。
mem.ja: Henry turned off the light, and 8月 finished the song in the dark.
mem.ko: 헨리가 빛을 끝어, 오거스트가 노래를 어둠 속에서 끝냈다.
mem.es: Henry turned off the light, and August finished the song in the dark.

t.en: One More Morning
t.ja: One More 朝
t.es: One More Morning

goal.en: Ask for one morning, not forever
goal.zh: 只求一个早晨，而不是永远
goal.ja: Ask for one morning, not forever
goal.es: Ask for one morning, not forever

place.en: The parlor, after the guests leave
place.ja: The parlor, after the guests leave
place.es: The parlor, after the guests leave

en: The guests are gone. The folding chairs are still out. August looks thinner at the edges, like a photo left too long in a window.
I can feel it now. Not a door. A draft. I think I could go.
I stack one chair, then stop. If I stack them all, it's over.
Don't ask him to stay. You know what you do to things you won't let go of. You fix them until they break.
Not because you asked. You should know the difference.
zh: 客人都走了，折叠椅还摆着。August的轮廓变淡了，像一张在窗台上晒得太久的照片。
我现在能感觉到了。不是一扇门，是一阵穿堂风。我想我可以走了。
我叠起一把椅子，然后停住了。要是全叠完，就结束了。
别求他留下。你知道你会怎么对待放不下的东西：一直修，修到它坏掉。
不是因为你开口了。你该分得清这两者。
ja: The guests are gone. The folding chairs are still out. 8月 looks thinner at the edges, like a photo left too long in a window.
I can feel it now. Not a door. A draft. I think I could go.
I stack one chair, then stop. If I stack them all, it's over.
Don't ask him to stay. You know what you do to things you won't let go of. You fix them until they break.
Not because you asked. You should know the difference.
ko: 손님들이 간다. 접이식 의자가 여전히 밖에 있다. 오거스트는 창에 너무 오래 왼쪽 사진처럼 가장자리에서 더 얇아 보인다.
난 지금 그것을 느낄 수 있어. 문이 아니야. 초안. 난 내가 갈 수 있을 것 같아.
난 의자를 쌓다 하면, 멈춰. 만약 난 그들을 모두 쌓으면, 그건 끝이야.
그에게 머물도록 묻지 마. 당신이 뭘 하는지 알아, 당신이 놓지 않을 것들에게. 당신이 그들이 부술 때까지 고친다.
한 개. 왜냐하면 난 그것을 원해.
당신이 물어봤다고 해서가 아니야. 당신이 그 차이를 알아야 해.
es: The guests are gone. The folding chairs are still out. August looks thinner at the edges, like a photo left too long in a window.
I can feel it now. Not a door. A draft. I think I could go.
I stack one chair, then stop. If I stack them all, it's over.
Don't ask him to stay. You know what you do to things you won't let go of. You fix them until they break.
Not because you asked. You should know the difference.

ask.en: How does Henry spend the last night?
ask.zh: Henry要怎么度过这最后一夜？
ask.ja: どのように does Henry spend the last night?
ask.es: How does Henry spend the last night?

t.en: Tell him why one morning matters.
t.zh: 告诉他，一个早晨为什么重要。
t.ja: Tell him why one morning matters.
t.es: Tell him why one morning matters.

en: My dad went at 4 AM in a hospital hallway. I was in the parking garage. I never got a morning.
I sit in the chair he didn't stack. I stay until he stops talking. Then I stay longer.
zh: 我爸是凌晨四点在医院走廊里走的。那时我在停车场。我没能等到一个早晨。
我坐在他没叠的那把椅子上，一直待到他说完。然后又多待了一会儿。
ja: My dad went at 4 AM in a hospital hallway. I was in the parking garage. I never got a morning.
I sit in the chair he didn't stack. I stay until he stops talking. Then I stay longer.
ko: 내 아버지가 병원 복도에서 오전 4시에 빨리 갔어. 난 주차 차고에 있었어. 난 절대 아침을 받지 못했어.
난 그가 쌓지 않은 의자에 앉다. 난 그가 말하는 것을 멈출 때까지 있다. 그럼 난 더 오래 있다.
es: My dad went at 4 AM in a hospital hallway. I was in the parking garage. I never got a morning.
I sit in the chair he didn't stack. I stay until he stops talking. Then I stay longer.

mem.en: Henry told August about missing his father's last morning; August stayed with him through the night.
mem.zh: Henry向August说起没能陪父亲度过最后一个早晨；August陪了他一整夜。
mem.ja: Henry told 8月 about missing his father's last morning; 8月 stayed with him through the night.
mem.ko: 헨리가 오거스트에게 그의 아버지의 마지막 아침을 놓치는 것에 대해 말했다. 오거스트가 밤새 그와 함께 있었다.
mem.es: Henry told August about missing his father's last morning; August stayed with him through the night.

t.en: Keep it light: plan a breakfast.
t.zh: 轻松一点：计划一顿早餐。
t.ja: 保つ it light: plan a breakfast.
t.ko: 그것을 가볍게 유지하다: 아침 식사를 계획하다.
t.es: Keep it light: plan a breakfast.

en: Then I'm making pancakes you can't eat. You'll watch and suffer.
Blueberry. I want to smell them. I can still do that, a little.
Henry sets an alarm for 5:30 and a bag of frozen blueberries on the counter to thaw, like a promise.
zh: 那我就做你吃不到的松饼。你只能看着受罪。
蓝莓的。我想闻闻。这个我还能做到一点。
Henry定了五点半的闹钟，又把一袋冷冻蓝莓放在台面上解冻，像许下一个承诺。
ja: Then I'm making pancakes you can't eat. You'll watch and suffer.
Blueberry. I want to smell them. I can still do that, a little.
Henry sets an alarm for 5:30 and a bag of frozen blueberries on the counter to thaw, like a promise.
ko: 그럼 난 당신이 먹을 수 없는 팬케이크를 만들 거야. 당신이 보고 고통받을 거야.
블루베리. 난 그들을 냄새 맡고 싶어. 난 여전히 조금 그럴 수 있어.
헨리는 오전 5시 30분 알람을 설정한다, 그리고 냉동 블루베리 가방을 카운터에, 해동하려고, 약속처럼.
es: Then I'm making pancakes you can't eat. You'll watch and suffer.
Blueberry. I want to smell them. I can still do that, a little.
Henry sets an alarm for 5:30 and a bag of frozen blueberries on the counter to thaw, like a promise.

mem.en: Henry and August planned a blueberry pancake breakfast August could only smell.
mem.zh: Henry和August约好一顿蓝莓松饼早餐，August只能闻闻香味。
mem.ja: Henry and 8月 planned a blueberry pancake breakfast 8月 could only smell.
mem.ko: 헨리와 오거스트는 블루베리 팬케이크 아침 식사를 계획했다, 오거스트가 오직 냄새맡을 수 있었던.
mem.es: Henry and August planned a blueberry pancake breakfast August could only smell.

t.en: Go to bed; let morning come on its own.
t.zh: 去睡觉，让早晨自己到来。
t.ja: 行く to bed; let morning come on its own.
t.ko: 침대로 가다. 아침이 자신의 것을 올 수 있게 하다.
t.es: Go to bed; let morning come on its own.

en: I'm not going to watch the clock with you. I'll see you when I see you.
Henry sleeps. At 5 AM, the radiator in his room clanks twice, in the rhythm of the song's first line.
zh: 我不想陪你盯着钟。该见面的时候自然会见。
Henry睡了。清晨五点，他房里的暖气片当当响了两下，正是那首歌第一句的节奏。
ja: I'm not going to watch the clock with you. I'll see you when I see you.
Henry sleeps. At 5 AM, the radiator in his room clanks twice, in the rhythm of the song's first line.
ko: 난 당신과 함께 시계를 보지 않을 거야. 난 당신이 볼 때 당신을 봐.
헨리가 잔다. 오전 5시에, 그의 방의 라디에이터가 두 번 부딪힌다, 노래의 첫 줄의 리듬으로.
es: I'm not going to watch the clock with you. I'll see you when I see you.
Henry sleeps. At 5 AM, the radiator in his room clanks twice, in the rhythm of the song's first line.

mem.en: Henry slept instead of keeping vigil; August woke him at 5 AM with the song's rhythm on the radiator.
mem.zh: Henry没有守夜而是去睡了；清晨五点，August在暖气片上敲出歌的节奏叫醒了他。
mem.ja: Henry slept instead of keeping vigil; 8月 woke him at 5 AM with the song's rhythm on the radiator.
mem.ko: 헨리가 깨어난 대신 잤어. 오거스트가 라디에이터에 노래의 리듬으로 오전 5시에 깨웠어.
mem.es: Henry slept instead of keeping vigil; August woke him at 5 AM with the song's rhythm on the radiator.

t.en: The Last Morning
t.ja: The Last 朝
t.es: The Last Morning

goal.en: Ask to keep the song, and let him go for real
goal.zh: 请求保留这首歌，并真正放他走
goal.ja: Ask to keep the song, and let him go for real
goal.ko: 노래를 유지하기를 묻다, 그리고 진짜로 그를 보내다
goal.es: Ask to keep the song, and let him go for real

en: Light comes in low over the lake. Henry doesn't close the curtain. He thought about it. He kept his hand off the cord.
I can miss you and do that.
Then the room was not a waste.
Somewhere there's an ad that says you can talk to your loved ones again. I'll never click it. He was here. That's the whole receipt.
zh: 晨光低低地越过湖面照进来。Henry没有拉上窗帘。他想过，但手没有碰那根绳子。
我可以一边想你，一边活下去。
那这个房间就没有白等。
总有广告说能让你和逝去的人再说上话。我永远不会点开。他来过，这就是全部的凭证。
ja: 光 comes in low over the lake. Henry doesn't close the curtain. He thought about it. He kept his hand off the cord.
I can miss you and do that.
Then the room was not a waste.
Somewhere there's an ad that says you can talk to your loved ones again. I'll never click it. He was here. That's the whole receipt.
ko: 빛이 낮게 호수에서 들어온다. 헨리가 커튼을 닫지 않는다. 그는 그것에 대해 생각했다. 그는 코드에서 손을 유지했다.
난 당신을 놓치고 그것을 할 수 있어.
어딘가에 광고가 있어, 당신이 당신의 사랑하는 사람과 다시 말할 수 있다고 말해. 난 절대 그것을 클릭하지 않을 거야. 그가 여기 있었어. 그건 전체 영수증이야.
es: Light comes in low over the lake. Henry doesn't close the curtain. He thought about it. He kept his hand off the cord.
I can miss you and do that.
Then the room was not a waste.
Somewhere there's an ad that says you can talk to your loved ones again. I'll never click it. He was here. That's the whole receipt.

ask.en: What does Henry say before the light gets high?
ask.zh: 趁太阳还没升高，Henry要说什么？
ask.ja: 何 does Henry say before the light gets high?
ask.ko: 헨리는 빛이 높아지기 전에 뭘 말하는가?
ask.es: What does Henry say before the light gets high?

t.en: Tell him you love him, with no conditions.
t.zh: 告诉他你爱他，不附带任何条件。
t.ja: Tell him you love him, with no conditions.
t.ko: 그에게 당신이 그를 사랑한다고 말하다, 조건 없이.
t.es: Tell him you love him, with no conditions.

en: I think I'm in love with you. That's not a request. It's just true, and you should hear it once.
I heard it. I'm keeping it. That's allowed, isn't it? Taking something with me?
I put the wind against his cheek. It's the most I have. It's everything I have.
zh: 我想我爱上你了。这不是请求，只是事实。你该听我说一次。
我听到了，我会带走它。可以的吧？带点东西走。
我让风贴上他的脸颊。这是我能给的最多了，也是我的全部。
ja: I think I'm in love with you. That's not a request. It's just true, and you should hear it once.
I heard it. I'm keeping it. That's allowed, isn't it? Taking something with me?
I put the wind against his cheek. It's the most I have. It's everything I have.
ko: 난 당신을 사랑하는 중이라고 생각해. 그건 요청이 아니야. 그건 단지 참이고, 당신이 그걸 한 번 들어야 해.
난 그걸 들었어. 난 그걸 유지하고 있어. 그건 허락되어 있지, 않아? 나와 함께 뭔가를 가져가?
난 그의 뺨에 바람을 놓는다. 그건 내가 가장 많은 것이야. 그건 내가 가진 모든 것이야.
es: I think I'm in love with you. That's not a request. It's just true, and you should hear it once.
I heard it. I'm keeping it. That's allowed, isn't it? Taking something with me?
I put the wind against his cheek. It's the most I have. It's everything I have.

mem.en: Henry told August he loved him without asking him to stay; August said he'd take it with him and touched his face with the wind.
mem.zh: Henry说他爱August，却没有求他留下；August说会把这句话带走，并用风轻触他的脸。
mem.ja: Henry told August he loved him without 聞く him to stay; August said he'd take it with him and touched his face with the wind.
mem.ko: 헨리가 오거스트에게 그가 유령을 그대로 두고 그를 사랑한다고 말했다. 오거스트가 그걸 가져갈 거라고 말했고, 바람으로 그의 얼굴을 건드렸다.
mem.es: Henry told August he loved him without asking him to stay; August said he'd take it with him and touched his face with the wind.

t.en: Tell him he doesn't have to go today.
t.ja: Tell him he doesn't have to go today.
t.ko: 그가 오늘 가지 않아도 돼라고 말하다.
t.es: Tell him he doesn't have to go today.

en: The draft will still be there next week. You don't owe anyone your leaving. Not even the song.
zh: 那阵风下周还会在。你不欠谁一次离开，连那首歌也不欠。
ja: The draft will still be there next week. You don't owe anyone your leaving. Not even the song.
ko: 초안은 다음 주에도 여전히 있을 거야. 당신은 누구든지 당신이 가는 것을 빚지지 않아. 심지어 노래도.
es: The draft will still be there next week. You don't owe anyone your leaving. Not even the song.

mem.en: Henry told August he could leave when he was ready, on a real deadline but not today's.
mem.zh: Henry告诉August，可以等准备好再走：有期限，但不是今天。
mem.ja: Henry told 8月 he could leave when he was ready, on a real deadline but not today's.
mem.ko: 헨리가 오거스트에게 그가 준비가 될 때 떠날 수 있다고 말했다, 실제 마감에, 그러나 오늘의가 아니다.
mem.es: Henry told August he could leave when he was ready, on a real deadline but not today's.

t.en: Thank him, as a friend.
t.ja: Thank him, as a friend.
t.es: Thank him, as a friend.

en: I don't think what I feel is romance. I think you're the best roommate I ever had, and you never paid rent.
zh: 我想我对你的感觉不是爱情。我觉得你是我遇过最好的室友，虽然你从没交过房租。
ja: I don't think what I feel is romance. I think you're the best roommate I ever had, and you never paid rent.
ko: 난 내가 느끼는 게 로맨스라고 생각하지 않아. 난 당신이 최고의 룸메이트라고 생각해, 난 절대 가져본 적 없고, 그리고 당신이 절대 세를 내지 않았어.
es: I don't think what I feel is romance. I think you're the best roommate I ever had, and you never paid rent.

mem.en: Henry thanked August as a friend and said plainly that what he felt wasn't romance.
mem.zh: Henry以朋友的身份感谢August，并坦白说自己的感情不是爱情。
mem.ja: Henry thanked 8月 as a friend and said plainly that what he felt wasn't romance.
mem.ko: 헨리가 오거스트에게 친구로 감사했고, 그가 느끼는 것이 로맨스가 아니라고 명확히 말했다.
mem.es: Henry thanked August as a friend and said plainly that what he felt wasn't romance.

t.en: The Porch Light
t.ja: The Porch 光
t.es: The Porch Light

goal.en: Choose the goodbye, or a little more time with an end date
goal.zh: 选择道别，或是一段有期限的相伴
goal.ja: Choose the goodbye, or a little more time with an end date
goal.ko: 안녕, 또는 끝 날짜와 조금 더 시간을 선택하다
goal.es: Choose the goodbye, or a little more time with an end date

en: The porch light is still on from last night. It's in the song. Henry reaches for the switch and doesn't flip it yet.
Leave it. I wrote that line about a light somebody forgot to turn off for me.
I stand on the porch step. The sun comes through me like I'm a screen door.
Whatever happens next, this happened. Nobody can refund it. Nobody can sell it back to me either.
Out on the lake, the fog is lifting. There's one choice left, and it isn't anyone's to buy.
zh: 门廊灯从昨晚一直亮到现在。它就在那首歌里。Henry伸手去摸开关，还没有按下去。
别关。那句歌词写的就是一盏有人忘了替我关掉的灯。
我站在门廊台阶上。阳光穿过我，像穿过一扇纱门。
不管接下来怎样，这一切发生过。谁也退不了款，谁也没法把它再卖给我一次。
湖上的雾正在散。还剩最后一个选择，而它不属于任何能买卖的东西。
ja: The porch light is still on from last night. It's in the song. Henry reaches for the switch and doesn't flip it yet.
去る it. I wrote that line about a light somebody forgot to turn off for me.
I stand on the porch step. The sun comes through me like I'm a screen door.
Whatever happens next, this happened. Nobody can refund it. Nobody can sell it back to me either.
Out on the lake, the fog is lifting. There's one choice left, and it isn't anyone's to buy.
ko: 현관등이 어제 밤부터 여전히 켜져 있다. 그건 노래에 있어. 헨리가 스위치에 손을 뻗고, 아직 그것을 켠다 해제하지 않는다.
그것을 놓아. 난 내가 누군가 나를 위해 끄는 것을 잊은 빛에 대한 줄을 썼어.
난 포치 계단에 선다. 태양이 내를 통해 온다, 마치 난 화면문처럼.
뭐든지 다음 일어날지, 이것이 일어났다. 아무도 그것을 환불할 수 없어. 아무도 나한테 그것을 다시 팔 수도 없어.
호수에 밖에, 안개가 올라가고 있어. 그곳에 한 개의 선택이 남아, 그리고 그건 누구의 것도 아니야, 사도록.
es: The porch light is still on from last night. It's in the song. Henry reaches for the switch and doesn't flip it yet.
Leave it. I wrote that line about a light somebody forgot to turn off for me.
I stand on the porch step. The sun comes through me like I'm a screen door.
Whatever happens next, this happened. Nobody can refund it. Nobody can sell it back to me either.
Out on the lake, the fog is lifting. There's one choice left, and it isn't anyone's to buy.

ask.ja: どのように do they say goodbye?

t.en: Say everything, and let him go in the light.
t.zh: 把话说尽，让他在晨光里离开。
t.ja: Say everything, and let him go in the light.
t.ko: 모두 말하고, 그리고 그를 빛 속에서 가게 하다.
t.es: Say everything, and let him go in the light.

en: I loved you on day three. You were fighting the water heater, and losing.
Go. I've got your song, with your name on it. I've got an inn to run.
One more morning. I got it. Because I wanted it.
The wind touches Henry's hand once, and then the porch is just a porch. He leaves the light on anyway.
zh: 第三天我就爱上你了。你在跟热水器打架，还打输了。
走吧。你的歌我留着，署着你的名字。我还有一家旅馆要开。
再一个早晨。我得到了。因为我想要。
风最后一次碰了碰Henry的手，然后门廊就只是门廊了。他还是让那盏灯亮着。
ja: I loved you on day three. You were fighting the water heater, and losing.
行く. I've got your song, with your name on it. I've got an inn to run.
One more morning. I got it. Because I wanted it.
The wind touches Henry's hand once, and then the porch is just a porch. He leaves the light on anyway.
ko: 난 3일에 당신을 사랑했어. 당신이 온수기와 싸우고 있었어, 그리고 지고 있었어.
가. 난 당신의 노래를 가지고 있어, 당신의 이름으로. 난 여관을 운영해야 해.
한 개 더 아침. 난 그걸 얻었어. 왜냐하면 난 그것을 원했으니까.
바람이 헨리의 손에 한 번 건드린다, 그리고 그럼 포치는 그냥 포치다. 그는 여전히 빛을 켠다 놓아.
es: I loved you on day three. You were fighting the water heater, and losing.
Go. I've got your song, with your name on it. I've got an inn to run.
One more morning. I got it. Because I wanted it.
The wind touches Henry's hand once, and then the porch is just a porch. He leaves the light on anyway.

mem.en: August confessed and left in the morning light; Henry kept the song with August's name on it and went on living.
mem.zh: August坦白心意，在晨光中离开；Henry保留了署着August名字的歌，继续生活。
mem.ja: 8月 confessed and left in the morning light; Henry kept the song with 8月's name on it and went on living.
mem.ko: 오거스트가 고백했고, 아침 빛 속에서 떠났어. 헨리가 오거스트의 이름으로 노래를 유지했고, 계속 살았다.
mem.es: August confessed and left in the morning light; Henry kept the song with August's name on it and went on living.

t.en: Ask him to stay until first snow, and write.
t.zh: 请他留到初雪，一起写歌。
t.ja: Ask him to stay until first snow, and write.
t.ko: 첫 눈까지 머물 것을 묻다, 그리고 쓰다.
t.es: Ask him to stay until first snow, and write.

en: Not forever. Until the first snow. Write something with me that isn't about dying.
The room board says AUGUST, CO-WRITER. The end date is written in pen, not dry-erase. They both agreed to that.
zh: 不是永远。留到下第一场雪。跟我写一首不是关于死亡的歌。
房态板上写着：AUGUST，合作词曲人。结束日期是用钢笔写的，不是白板笔。这是两人都同意的。
ja: Not forever. Until the first snow. Write something with me that isn't about dying.
The room board says AUGUST, CO-WRITER. The end date is written in pen, not dry-erase. They both agreed to that.
ko: 영원히 아니다. 첫 눈까지. 죽음에 대해 가 아닌 뭔가를 나와 함께 쓰다.
방 보드는 오거스트, 공동 저자라고 한다. 마감일이 건식 지우개에 빵에 적혀 있어. 둘 다 그것에 동의했어.
es: Not forever. Until the first snow. Write something with me that isn't about dying.
The room board says AUGUST, CO-WRITER. The end date is written in pen, not dry-erase. They both agreed to that.

mem.en: August chose to stay until the first snow as Henry's co-writer, with the end date agreed and written in pen.
mem.zh: August决定作为Henry的合作词曲人留到初雪，结束日期双方同意，并用钢笔写下。
mem.ja: 8月 chose to stay until the first snow as Henry's co-writer, with the end date agreed and written in pen.
mem.ko: 오거스트가 첫 눈까지 머물기로 선택했다, 헨리의 공동 저자로, 마감일이 동의되고 빵에 적혀 있어.
mem.es: August chose to stay until the first snow as Henry's co-writer, with the end date agreed and written in pen.

t.en: Say goodbye as friends, on the porch.
t.zh: 在门廊上，以朋友的身份道别。
t.ja: Say goodbye as friends, on the porch.
t.es: Say goodbye as friends, on the porch.

en: You were a friend when I needed one. Go easy.
You threw me the best show of my life, and I'm dead. That's a real review.
Four chairs, Henry. It was enough.
August goes the way fog goes, with no moment you can point to. The fourth chair stays out in the parlor all winter.
zh: 我需要朋友的时候，你就是那个朋友。走好。
你为我办了这辈子最好的一场演出，而我已经死了。这是真心的好评。
August像雾一样离开，找不到哪一刻能指着说就是现在。第四把椅子在客厅里摆了一整个冬天。
ja: You were a friend when I needed one. 行く easy.
You threw me the best show of my life, and I'm dead. That's a real review.
Four chairs, Henry. It was enough.
8月 goes the way fog goes, with no moment you can point to. The fourth chair stays out in the parlor all winter.
ko: 당신이 친구였어, 난 한 명이 필요했어. 쉽게 가.
당신이 나에게 내 삶의 최고의 쇼를 던졌어, 그리고 난 죽었어. 그건 실제 리뷰야.
오거스트가 안개가 가는 방식으로, 당신이 포인트할 수 없는 순간과 함께 간다. 4번째 의자는 모든 겨울 거실에 있어.
es: You were a friend when I needed one. Go easy.
You threw me the best show of my life, and I'm dead. That's a real review.
Four chairs, Henry. It was enough.
August goes the way fog goes, with no moment you can point to. The fourth chair stays out in the parlor all winter.

mem.en: Henry and August said goodbye as friends; the fourth chair stayed out all winter.
mem.zh: Henry和August以朋友身份道别；第四把椅子在客厅摆了一整个冬天。
mem.ja: Henry and 8月 said goodbye as friends; the fourth chair stayed out all winter.
mem.ko: 헨리와 오거스트가 친구로 안녕이라고 말했어. 4번째 의자가 모든 겨울 밖에 있어.
mem.es: Henry and August said goodbye as friends; the fourth chair stayed out all winter.

t.en: One More Morning
t.ja: One More 朝
t.es: One More Morning

txt.en: The song is finished and the confession is said. August leaves in the morning light because he's ready, not because anyone paid or pleaded. Henry keeps the song with August's name on it and keeps living. It isn't forever, and it was never meant to be.
txt.zh: 歌唱完了，心意也说出口了。August在晨光中离开，因为他准备好了，而不是有人付钱或哀求。Henry保留了署着August名字的歌，继续生活。这不是永远，也从来不必是永远。
txt.ja: The song is finished and the confession is said. 8月 leaves in the morning light because he's ready, not because anyone paid or pleaded. Henry keeps the song with 8月's name on it and keeps living. It isn't forever, and it was never meant to be.
txt.ko: 노래가 끝나고, 고백이 말해진다. 오거스트가 아침 빛 속에서 가, 왜냐하면 그가 준비됐으니까, 아무도 지불하거나 간청하지 않았으니까. 헨리가 오거스트의 이름으로 노래를 유지하고, 계속 산다. 그건 영원히가 아니고, 그건 절대 의도될 수 없었어.
txt.es: The song is finished and the confession is said. August leaves in the morning light because he's ready, not because anyone paid or pleaded. Henry keeps the song with August's name on it and keeps living. It isn't forever, and it was never meant to be.

line.en: One more morning. I got it. Because I wanted it.
line.zh: 再一个早晨。我得到了。因为我想要。
line.ja: One more morning. I got it. Because I wanted it.
line.ko: 한 개 더 아침. 난 그걸 얻었어. 왜냐하면 난 그것을 원했으니까.
line.es: One more morning. I got it. Because I wanted it.

t.en: Until the First Snow
t.ja: Until the First 雪
t.es: Until the First Snow

txt.en: August isn't ready to go, and Henry doesn't make him. They agree on a season, not a lifetime, and write songs together until the first snow. The end date is in pen. They both chose it.
txt.zh: August还没准备好离开，Henry也不逼他。两人约定的是一个季节，不是一辈子，一起写歌直到初雪。结束日期用钢笔写着，是他们一起选的。
txt.ja: 8月 isn't ready to go, and Henry doesn't make him. They agree on a season, not a lifetime, and write songs together until the first snow. The end date is in pen. They both chose it.
txt.ko: 오거스트가 가려고 준비되지 않았고, 헨리가 그를 강요하지 않아. 그들이 계절에 동의해, 영원히가 아니라, 그리고 첫 눈까지 함께 노래를 쓴다. 마감일이 빵에 있어. 그들이 둘 다 선택했어.
txt.es: August isn't ready to go, and Henry doesn't make him. They agree on a season, not a lifetime, and write songs together until the first snow. The end date is in pen. They both chose it.

line.en: Until the first snow. Then you open the window.
line.zh: 直到初雪。到时候，你替我开窗。
line.ja: Until the first snow. Then you open the window.
line.ko: 첫 눈까지. 그럼 당신이 창을 열어.
line.es: Until the first snow. Then you open the window.

t.en: Four Chairs Was Enough
t.ja: Four Chairs Was Enough
t.es: Four Chairs Was Enough

txt.en: Henry doesn't want romance, and he says so. He still gives August the show and a good goodbye, and they part as friends. The fourth chair stays out all winter.
txt.zh: Henry不想要爱情，也坦白说了。他还是为August办完了演出，好好道了别，两人以朋友身份分开。第四把椅子摆了一整个冬天。
txt.ja: Henry doesn't want romance, and he says so. He still gives 8月 the show and a good goodbye, and they part as friends. The fourth chair stays out all winter.
txt.ko: 헨리가 로맨스를 원하지 않아, 그리고 그가 그렇다고 말한다. 그는 여전히 오거스트에게 쇼를 주고, 좋은 안녕을, 그리고 그들이 친구로 떠난다. 4번째 의자가 모든 겨울 밖에 있어.
txt.es: Henry doesn't want romance, and he says so. He still gives August the show and a good goodbye, and they part as friends. The fourth chair stays out all winter.

line.en: Four chairs, Henry. It was enough.
line.ja: Four chairs, Henry. It was enough.
line.es: Four chairs, Henry. It was enough.

t.en: The Week Before the Show
t.ja: The 週 Before the Show
t.es: The Week Before the Show

d.en: Two extra scenes from rehearsal week: August teaching Henry to tune one string, and a rainy afternoon they spend arguing about a chorus. It adds time with August, never a way to bring him back.
d.zh: 排练周的两场额外戏：August教Henry调一根琴弦，还有一个下雨的午后，两人为副歌吵个不停。它让你多陪August一会儿，但绝不提供让他复活的方法。
d.ja: Two extra scenes from rehearsal week: 8月 teaching Henry to tune one string, and a rainy afternoon they spend arguing about a chorus. It adds time with 8月, never a way to bring him back.
d.ko: 리허설 주의 2개 추가 장면: 오거스트가 헨리에게 한 줄을 튜닝하는 것을 배우고, 그리고 습한 오후, 그들이 코러스에 대해 싸우는 데 보낸다. 그건 오거스트와 시간을 더한다, 절대 그를 다시 가져올 방법이 아니다.
d.es: Two extra scenes from rehearsal week: August teaching Henry to tune one string, and a rainy afternoon they spend arguing about a chorus. It adds time with August, never a way to bring him back.

polaroid.en: Four chairs in the lamplight, one of them empty, with your caption on the border
polaroid.zh: 灯光下的四把椅子，其中一把空着，边框上写着你的题字
polaroid.ja: Four chairs in the lamplight, one of them empty, with your caption on the border
polaroid.ko: 4개의 의자, 램프등, 하나가 비어있고, 경계에 당신의 캡션
polaroid.es: Four chairs in the lamplight, one of them empty, with your caption on the border

game.en: Tune the piano and keep rehearsal time. Playable in text mode.
game.zh: 修钢琴、跟排练节奏，文字模式也能完成
game.ja: Tune the piano and keep rehearsal time. Playable in text mode.
game.ko: 한 줄을 튜닝하고, 리허설 시간을 유지하다. 텍스트 모드에서 플레이가능.
game.es: Tune the piano and keep rehearsal time. Playable in text mode.

gift.en: Four plain invitation cards. No gift buys him another day.
gift.zh: 四张普通的邀请卡；没有任何礼物能为他换来多一天
gift.ja: Four plain invitation cards. No gift buys him another day.
gift.ko: 4개의 평이한 초대 카드. 아무 선물도 그에게 또 다른 날을 사지 못해.
gift.es: Four plain invitation cards. No gift buys him another day.

date.en: A timed midnight on the roof
date.ja: A timed midnight on the roof
date.es: A timed midnight on the roof

photo.en: The moved ladder, wind on a hand, four chairs
photo.zh: 被挪动的梯子、风拂过的手、四把椅子
photo.ja: The moved ladder, wind on a hand, four chairs
photo.ko: 옮겨진 사다리, 손 위의 바람, 4개의 의자
photo.es: The moved ladder, wind on a hand, four chairs

voice.en: August's original song in full, plus a short goodbye message
voice.zh: August的原创歌曲完整版，外加一段简短的告别留言
voice.ja: 8月's original song in full, plus a short goodbye message
voice.ko: 전체 오거스트의 원래 노래, 그리고 짧은 안녕 메시지
voice.es: August's original song in full, plus a short goodbye message

room.en: Four cards, the licensed lyrics, one empty chair
room.zh: 四张卡片、授权的歌词、一把空椅子
room.ja: Four cards, the licensed lyrics, one empty chair
room.ko: 4개의 카드, 허가된 가사, 한 개의 빈 의자
room.es: Four cards, the licensed lyrics, one empty chair

allowed.en: Nobody shows up: one or more guests cancel the day of the show
allowed.zh: 观众缺席：演出当天有一位或几位客人来不了
allowed.ja: Nobody shows up: one or more guests cancel the day of the show
allowed.ko: 아무도 나타나지 않는다: 한 명 이상의 손님이 쇼 날에 취소한다
allowed.es: Nobody shows up: one or more guests cancel the day of the show

allowed.en: The piano goes sour mid-song and August has to keep going
allowed.zh: 唱到一半钢琴突然走调，August得继续唱下去
allowed.ja: The piano goes sour mid-song and 8月 has to keep going
allowed.ko: 피아노가 노래 중간에 신맛이 나고, 오거스트가 계속 가야 한다
allowed.es: The piano goes sour mid-song and August has to keep going

allowed.en: Add a third person who can see August (give their name, how they got in, and what they know)
allowed.zh: 加入一个能看见August的第三人（需说明姓名、怎么进来的、知道多少）
allowed.ja: Add a third person who can see 8月 (give their name, how they got in, and what they know)
allowed.ko: 오거스트가 볼 수 있는 세 번째 사람을 추가하다 (그들의 이름, 그들이 어떻게 들어왔는지, 그리고 그들이 뭘 알고 있는지)
allowed.es: Add a third person who can see August (give their name, how they got in, and what they know)

au.en: AU: August is alive and books the parlor show for real. A separate story that doesn't overwrite the goodbye.
au.zh: AU：August还活着，真的订下了客厅的演出。这是独立故事，不覆盖原本的告别。
au.ja: AU: 8月 is alive and books the parlor show for real. A separate story that doesn't overwrite the goodbye.
au.ko: AU: 오거스트는 산다, 그리고 거실 쇼를 진짜로 예약한다. 별개의 이야기, 안녕을 덮어 쓰지 않다.
au.es: AU: August is alive and books the parlor show for real. A separate story that doesn't overwrite the goodbye.

au.en: AU: Eleven years earlier, the night the original show was booked, and Henry is the one in the audience
au.zh: AU：回到十一年前原定演出的那个夜晚，Henry是台下的观众
au.ja: AU: Eleven years earlier, the night the original show was booked, and Henry is the one in the audience
au.ko: AU: 11년 전, 원래 쇼가 예약된 밤, 그리고 헨리는 관객에 있는 하나다
au.es: AU: Eleven years earlier, the night the original show was booked, and Henry is the one in the audience
